title.zh: 卷50 列傳第15 宇文慶 李禮成 元孝矩 郭榮 龐晃 李安
title.en: Volume 50 Biographies 15: Yu Wenqing, Li Licheng, Yuan Xiaoju, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, Li An
title.raw: 卷50 列傳第15 宇文慶 李禮成 元孝矩 郭榮 龐晃 李安 Volume 50 Biographies 15: Yu Wenqing, Li Licheng, Yuan Xiaoju, Guo Rong, Pang Huang, Li An

sentences.zh: 隋書卷五十列傳第十五

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 50, Biographies, Section 15
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 50, Biographies 15

sentences.zh: ○宇文慶

translations.literal: ○ Yu Wen Qing
translations.idiomatic: ● Yu Wen Qing

sentences.zh: 宇文慶，字神慶，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wen Qing, courtesy name Shenqing, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen Qing, whose courtesy name was Shenqing, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖金殿，魏征南大將軍，仕曆五州刺史、安吉侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jindian was the Northern Wei's General Who Conquers the South; in office he successively governed five prefectures and held the title Marquis of Anji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jindian had served as the Northern Wei's General Who Conquers the South, governing five prefectures in succession and holding the title Marquis of Anji.

sentences.zh: 父顯和，夏州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xianhe was Governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianhe had been governor of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 慶沉深有器局，少以聰敏見知。

translations.literal: Qing was deep and steady and possessed breadth of character; in youth he became known for keen intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was sober and far-sighted, with a capacity for large affairs, and was recognized early on for his quick mind.

sentences.zh: 周初，受業東觀，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhou he studied at the Eastern Pavilion and gained considerable acquaintance with the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Northern Zhou he studied at the Eastern Pavilion and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 既而謂人曰：「書足記姓名而已，安能久事筆硯，為腐儒之業！

translations.literal: Before long he said to others: "Books are enough merely to record one's name—how could one long devote oneself to brush and inkstone and make the work of a pedantic scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long he told people, "Books are only good for keeping your name on record—how could I spend my life at a desk and become one of those stale bookworms!"

sentences.zh: 」于時文州民夷相聚為亂，慶應募從征。

translations.literal: At that time the tribal peoples of Wen Prefecture gathered and rebelled together; Qing volunteered and followed on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the tribal peoples of Wen Prefecture rose in revolt; Qing answered the call and joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊據保岩谷，徑路懸絕，慶束馬而進，襲破之，以功授都督。

translations.literal: The bandits held Baoyan Gorge; the paths were perpendicularly cut off. Qing bound up his horse and advanced, surprise-attacked and broke them, and for merit was appointed commander.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Baoyan Gorge, where the trail was sheer and impassable. Qing had his horse tethered and went in on foot, stormed them, and routed the force; for this he was made a military commander.

sentences.zh: 衛王直之鎮山南也，引為左右。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Zhi garrisoned the southern mountains, he took Qing into his personal retinue.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Zhi was posted to garrison the southern mountains, he brought Qing into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 慶善射，有膽氣，好格猛獸，直甚壯之。

translations.literal: Qing excelled at archery, had bold spirit, and loved grappling with fierce beasts; Zhi greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was an expert archer, bold in spirit, and fond of wrestling fierce beasts; the prince thought highly of his courage.

sentences.zh: 稍遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、柱國府掾。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Yitong of the Third Rank, and adjutant in the office of the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Yitong of the Third Rank, and an adjutant in the Chancellor of State's office.

sentences.zh: 及誅宇文護，慶有謀焉，進授驃騎大將軍，加開府。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, Qing had a hand in the plot; he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and given the privilege of an independent command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was killed, Qing had helped plan the move; he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and granted an independent command.

sentences.zh: 後從武帝攻河陰，先登攀堞，與賊短兵接戰，良久，中石乃墜，絕而後蘇。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu in attacking Heyin, was first to climb the ramparts, fought the enemy at close quarters for a long while, was struck by a stone and fell, lost consciousness, and afterward revived.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Wu in the attack on Heyin, was the first to scale the walls, and fought the enemy hand to hand for a long time until a stone struck him and he fell; he lost consciousness but later came to.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「卿之餘勇，可以賈人也。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "Your remaining courage could be sold for a price."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, saying, "Even what courage you have left could be sold at a premium."

sentences.zh: 」複從武帝拔晉州。

translations.literal: Again he followed Emperor Wu in capturing Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Emperor Wu in the capture of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後齊師大至，慶與宇文憲輕騎而覘，卒與賊相遇，為賊所窘。

translations.literal: Afterward the Qi army arrived in great force; Qing and Yuwen Xian went out on light horse to reconnoiter, suddenly met the enemy, and were pressed hard.
translations.idiomatic: When a large Qi army arrived soon after, Qing and Yuwen Xian rode out on light horse to scout and suddenly ran into the enemy, who hemmed them in.

sentences.zh: 憲挺身而遁，慶退據汾橋，眾賊爭進，慶引弓射之，所中人馬必倒，賊乃稍卻。

translations.literal: Xian threw himself forward and escaped; Qing withdrew and held the Fen Bridge. The mass of bandits pressed forward in contention; Qing drew his bow and shot—whomever he hit, man or horse, necessarily fell; the bandits then drew back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian broke free and fled; Qing fell back to hold the Fen Bridge. As the enemy swarmed forward, Qing shot with his bow, and every man or horse he struck went down, until the rebels at last gave ground.

sentences.zh: 及破高緯，拔高壁，克并州，下信都，禽高湝，功並居最。

translations.literal: When Gao Wei was defeated, they took Gaobi, captured Bingzhou, reduced Xindu, and captured Gao Shaoji—Qing's merit ranked foremost among all.
translations.idiomatic: In the defeat of Gao Wei they took Gaobi, captured Bingzhou, reduced Xindu, and captured Gao Shaoji; Qing's achievements ranked first among all.

sentences.zh: 周武帝詔曰：「慶勳庸早著，英望華遠，出內之績，簡在朕心。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou issued an edict saying: "Qing's merit and service were early manifest; his heroic reputation shines far. His achievements at court and in the field are selected and kept in Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou issued an edict saying, "Qing's merit was evident early on, and his reputation shines far; his service at court and in the field has not escaped Our notice."

sentences.zh: 戎車自西，俱總行陣，東夏蕩定，實有茂功。

translations.literal: When the war chariots came from the west, he jointly commanded the marching armies; the pacification of eastern Xia was in truth a work of abundant merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies marched westward he shared command of the columns, and in pacifying the eastern regions he performed outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 高位縟禮，宜崇榮冊。

translations.literal: High rank and patterned rites—it is fitting to honor him with a glorious patent.
translations.idiomatic: High rank and ceremonial honors are what he deserves.

sentences.zh: 」於是進位大將軍，封汝南郡公，邑千六百戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Runan commandery, with a fief of 1,600 households.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Runan commandery with a fief of 1,600 households.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍總管擊延安反胡，平之，拜延州總管。

translations.literal: Soon as campaigning commander-in-chief he attacked the rebellious Hu of Yan'an, pacified them, and was appointed Governor-General of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as campaigning commander-in-chief, he attacked the rebellious Hu of Yan'an, pacified them, and was appointed governor-general of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄轉甯州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Governor-General of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to governor-general of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，複以行軍總管南征江表。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, again as campaigning commander-in-chief he campaigned south against the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was still Chancellor, Qing again served as campaigning commander-in-chief in the southern expedition against the Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 師次白帝，征還，以勞進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baidi; he was recalled from campaign and, for his labors, was advanced to Supreme Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Baidi; he was recalled from the campaign and promoted to Supreme Grand General for his exertions.

sentences.zh: 高祖與慶有舊，甚見親待，令督丞相軍事，委以心腹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Qing had old ties; he was greatly favored and treated with intimacy, ordered to supervise the Chancellor's military affairs, and entrusted as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Qing were old acquaintances; Qing was treated with exceptional intimacy, put in charge of the Chancellor's military affairs, and trusted as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 尋加柱國。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given the rank of Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made a Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜左武衛將軍，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed General of the Left Martial Guards and advanced to Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang reign he was appointed General of the Left Martial Guards and promoted to Supreme Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 數年，出除涼州總管。

translations.literal: After several years he went out and was dismissed as Governor-General of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was sent out as governor-general of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，征還，不任以職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled from campaign and given no further office.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was recalled and given no further duties.

sentences.zh: 初，上潛龍時，嘗從容與慶言及天下事，上謂慶曰：「天元實無積德，視其相貌，壽亦不長。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor was still in obscurity, he once spoke at leisure with Qing about affairs under Heaven. The Emperor said to Qing: "The Tianyuan Emperor in truth has accumulated no virtue; judging from his appearance, his lifespan will not be long either."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the Emperor was still only a rising power, he once spoke frankly with Qing about the state of the realm. He told Qing, "The Tianyuan Emperor has built up no real virtue, and to judge by his looks he will not live long either."

sentences.zh: 加以法令繁苛，耽恣聲色，以吾觀之，殆將不久。

translations.literal: Moreover, laws and ordinances are numerous and harsh, and he indulges without restraint in music and women—in my view, his end will come before long.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that, his laws are harsh and excessive, and he gives himself over to pleasure without restraint; in my view, he will not last much longer.

sentences.zh: 又複諸侯微弱，各令就國，曾無深根固本之計。

translations.literal: Again, the feudal lords are weak; each has been ordered to go to his state, and there has never been any plan to plant deep roots and secure the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the feudal princes have been weakened, each sent off to his own domain, with never a plan to plant deep roots and secure the foundation.

sentences.zh: 羽翮既剪，何能及遠哉！

translations.literal: Once the wings and pinions are clipped, how can one reach far!
translations.idiomatic: Once their wings are clipped, how far can they fly!

sentences.zh: 尉迥貴戚，早著聲望，國家有釁，必為亂階。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jiong is of noble kin and early won renown; if the state has a crack, he will surely become the stairway to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong is a noble kinsman who won renown early on; if trouble opens in the state, he is sure to become the first step toward rebellion.

sentences.zh: 然智量庸淺，子弟輕佻，貪而少惠，終致亡滅。

translations.literal: Yet his wisdom and capacity are mediocre and shallow, his sons and younger brothers frivolous; he is greedy and lacking in kindness, and in the end will bring on ruin and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his mind is shallow, his sons and brothers frivolous; he is greedy and lacking in generosity, and in the end will destroy himself.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難反覆之虜，亦非池內之物，變成俄頃，但輕薄無謀，未能為害，不過自竄江南耳。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan is a barbarian given to reversal; he too is not a creature to be kept in the pond. Change will come in an instant, but he is frivolous and without strategy, unable to do harm—no more than to flee on his own to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan is an unreliable foreigner, not someone who belongs in the inner circle; he may turn in a moment, but he is shallow and without strategy and cannot do real harm—at most he will flee south of the Yangtze on his own.

sentences.zh: 庸、蜀險隘，易生艱阻，王謙愚蠢，素無籌略，但恐為人所誤，不足為虞。

translations.literal: Yong and Shu are perilous and narrow, easily giving rise to hardship and obstruction; Wang Qian is stupid and from of old without stratagem—only I fear he may be misled by others; he is not enough to cause worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Shu are rugged and hard to pass, where trouble comes easily; Wang Qian is a fool who has never had a plan—he may only be led astray by others and is not worth worrying over.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，上言皆驗。

translations.literal: Before long, all the Emperor's words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, everything the Emperor had said came true.

sentences.zh: 及此，慶恐上遺忘，不復收用，欲見舊蒙恩顧，具錄前言為表而奏之曰：「臣聞智侔造化，二儀無以隱其靈；

translations.literal: At this point Qing feared the Emperor had forgotten him and would not again employ him; wishing to show he still enjoyed the old favor and regard, he fully recorded the earlier words in a memorial and presented it, saying: "Your servant has heard that when wisdom equals creation and transformation, the Two Principles cannot hide its spirit;"
translations.idiomatic: By then Qing feared the Emperor had forgotten him and would never call him back; hoping to remind him of their old bond, he set down their earlier conversation in a memorial and submitted it, writing, "I have heard that when wisdom rivals creation itself, heaven and earth cannot conceal its workings;"

sentences.zh: 明同日月，萬象不能藏其狀。

translations.literal: "when clarity is the same as sun and moon, the ten thousand phenomena cannot conceal their forms."
translations.idiomatic: "when insight matches the sun and moon, nothing under heaven can hide its true shape."

sentences.zh: 先天弗違，實聖人之體道；

translations.literal: "To go before Heaven and not be disobeyed is truly the sage's embodiment of the Way;"
translations.idiomatic: "To anticipate Heaven without being contradicted is how the sage embodies the Way;"

sentences.zh: 未萌見兆，諒達節之神機。

translations.literal: "to see the omen before it has sprouted is surely the divine mechanism of one who comprehends the key."
translations.idiomatic: "to read the signs before they appear is the divine insight of one who grasps the essential."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下特挺生知，徇齊誕禦，懷五嶽其猶輕，吞八荒而不梗，蘊妙見於胸襟，運奇謨於掌握。

translations.literal: "I bow and consider that Your Majesty was uniquely endowed with innate knowledge, followed the utmost in taking the throne, holds the Five Marchmounts as though they were light, swallows the eight wilds without choking, stores subtle insight in the breast, and turns wondrous stratagems in the palm."
translations.idiomatic: "I humbly consider that Your Majesty was born with extraordinary wisdom, took the throne in accord with the highest principle, holds the Five Marchmounts as lightly as pebbles and encompasses the eight directions without strain, keeps subtle insight in your breast, and turns brilliant stratagems in the palm of your hand."

sentences.zh: 臣以微賤，早逢天眷，不以庸下，親蒙推赤。

translations.literal: "Your servant, being mean and lowly, early encountered Heaven's favor; though unworthy and base, I personally received your opening of the heart."
translations.idiomatic: "I am humble and lowly, yet I met your favor early on; though I am unworthy, you opened your heart to me in person."

sentences.zh: 所奉成規，纖毫弗舛，尋惟聖慮，妙出蓍龜，驗一人之慶有徵，實天子之言無戲。

translations.literal: "The rules you entrusted to me have not erred by a hair's breadth. Reflecting on your sacred thought, it is wondrous beyond divining stalks and tortoise shells; verifying that this one man's Qing had proof—the Son of Heaven's words were in truth no jest."
translations.idiomatic: "The predictions you entrusted to me have not missed by a hair. Reflecting on your sacred foresight, it surpasses any divination; to see that what you told me alone has come true proves that the Son of Heaven's words are never spoken in jest."

sentences.zh: 臣親聞親見，實榮實喜。

translations.literal: "Your servant heard it in person and saw it in person—truly honored, truly delighted."
translations.idiomatic: "I heard it with my own ears and have seen it with my own eyes—this is honor and joy indeed."

sentences.zh: 」上省表大悅，下詔曰：「朕之與公，本來親密，懷抱委曲，無所不盡。

translations.literal: The Emperor, on reading the memorial, was greatly pleased and issued an edict saying: "Between Us and you, sir, there was intimacy from the start; what lay in Our breast, every twist and turn, We held back nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial with great delight and issued an edict saying, "Between us there has always been intimacy; what lay in my heart, every twist and turn, I held back nothing from you."

sentences.zh: 話言歲久，尚能記憶，今覽表奏，方悟昔談。

translations.literal: "Our words are years old, yet you can still remember them. Reading your memorial today, We have only now grasped Our talk of old."
translations.idiomatic: "Our conversation was years ago, yet you still remember it. Reading your memorial today, I have only now recalled what we said then."

sentences.zh: 何謂此言，遂成實錄。

translations.literal: "Who would have thought these words would become a verified record!"
translations.idiomatic: "Who would have thought those words would become a verified record!"

sentences.zh: 古人之先知禍福，明可信也，朕言之驗，自是偶然。

translations.literal: "The ancients' foreknowledge of fortune and calamity is clearly believable; that Our words were verified was merely chance."
translations.idiomatic: "The ancients' foreknowledge of fortune and disaster is clearly credible; that my words came true was mere chance."

sentences.zh: 公乃不忘，彌表誠節，深感至意，嘉尚無已。

translations.literal: "Yet you, sir, have not forgotten, and all the more display sincere loyalty. We are deeply moved by your utmost intent and praise and esteem you without end."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet you have not forgotten, and all the more show your loyal devotion. I am deeply moved by your sincerity and cannot praise you enough."

sentences.zh: 」自是上每加優禮。

translations.literal: From then on the Emperor continually added preferential treatment.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Emperor treated him with ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子靜禮，初為太子千牛備身，尋尚高祖女廣平公主，授儀同，安德縣公，邑千五百戶，後為熊州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Jingli at first served as a thousand-bushel attendant of the Heir Apparent; soon he married Emperor Gaozu's daughter, the Princess of Guangping, was given Yitong rank, made Duke of Ande county with a fief of 1,500 households, and later became Governor of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingli first served as an attendant in the Heir Apparent's guard, then married Emperor Gaozu's daughter, the Princess of Guangping; he was given Yitong rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Ande county with a fief of 1,500 households, and later became governor of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 先慶卒。

translations.literal: He died before Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his father Qing.

sentences.zh: 子協，曆武賁郎將、右翊衛將軍，宇文化及之亂遇害。

translations.literal: His son Xie successively held the posts of Lang General of the Martial Guards and General of the Right Wing Guards; he was killed in the disorder of Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie served successively as Lang General of the Martial Guards and General of the Right Wing Guards and was killed in the uprising of Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 協弟皛，字婆羅門，大業之世，少養宮中。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Xiao, courtesy name Boluomen, in the Daye era was reared from youth within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Xiao, whose courtesy name was Boluomen, was raised in the palace from boyhood during the Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 後為千牛左右，煬帝甚親昵之。

translations.literal: Later he became an attendant of the thousand-bushel guard; Emperor Yang was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became an attendant in the imperial guard, and Emperor Yang favored him with exceptional intimacy.

sentences.zh: 每有遊宴，皛必侍從，至於出入臥內，伺察六宮，往來不限門禁，其恩幸如此。

translations.literal: Whenever there were outings and banquets, Xiao necessarily attended; he even went in and out of the sleeping quarters, observed the Six Palaces, and came and went without limit of gate or prohibition—such was his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor went out or held a feast, Xiao was always at his side; he even entered the inner sleeping quarters, kept watch over the Six Palaces, and passed in and out without regard for the palace gates—such was the extent of his favor.

sentences.zh: 時人號曰宇文三郎。

translations.literal: People of the time called him the Third Son Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him Third Son Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 皛與宮人淫亂，至於妃嬪公主，亦有醜聲。

translations.literal: Xiao engaged in licentious disorder with palace women; even consorts and princesses had ugly rumors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao carried on licentious affairs with palace women, and even consorts and princesses were rumored to be involved.

sentences.zh: 蕭後言於帝，皛聞而懼，數日不敢見。

translations.literal: Empress Xiao spoke of it to the Emperor; Xiao heard and was afraid, and for several days did not dare appear before him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao reported this to the Emperor; when Xiao heard of it he was afraid and for several days did not dare show himself.

sentences.zh: 其兄協因奏曰：「皛今已壯，不可在宮掖。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xie thereupon memorialized, saying: "Xiao is now grown; he cannot remain in the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xie then memorialized, saying, "Xiao is grown now and should not remain in the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「皛安在？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Where is Xiao?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Where is Xiao?"

sentences.zh: 」協曰：「在朝堂。

translations.literal: Xie said: "He is in the audience hall."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "He is in the audience hall."

sentences.zh: 」帝不之罪，因召入，待之如初。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not blame him, and thereupon summoned him in and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not blame him, summoned him in, and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，皛時在玄覽門，覺變，將入奏，為門司所遏，不得時進。

translations.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Xiao was at the Xuanlan Gate; sensing the change, he was about to enter and report but was blocked by the gate officials and could not advance in time.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Xiao was at the Xuanlan Gate; sensing trouble, he tried to go in and report it but was stopped by the gate guards and could not get through in time.

sentences.zh: 會日瞑，宮門閉，退還所守。

translations.literal: It happened that the sun set and the palace gates closed; he withdrew and returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell and the palace gates closed; he withdrew to his post.

sentences.zh: 俄而難作，皛與五十人赴之，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Shortly the calamity broke out; Xiao and fifty men rushed to the scene and were killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crisis broke out; Xiao rushed there with fifty men and was killed by the mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: ○李禮成

translations.literal: ○ Li Licheng
translations.idiomatic: ● Li Licheng

sentences.zh: 李禮成，字孝諧，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Li Licheng, courtesy name Xiaoxie, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Licheng, whose courtesy name was Xiaoxie, came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 涼王暠之六世孫。

translations.literal: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Prince Liang Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Li Liang, Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 祖延實，魏司徒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanshi was Chancellor of State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanshi had been Chancellor of State of the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父彧，侍中。

translations.literal: His father Yu was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had been Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 禮成年七歲，與姑之子蘭陵太守滎陽鄭顥隨魏武帝入關。

translations.literal: When Licheng was seven years old, he followed his aunt's son Zheng Hao of Xingyang, Governor of Lanling, in entering the passes with Emperor Wu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Licheng was seven, he followed his aunt's son Zheng Hao of Xingyang, governor of Lanling, westward with Emperor Wu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 顥母每謂所親曰：「此兒平生未嘗回顧，當為重器耳。

translations.literal: Hao's mother often said to those close to her: "This boy in his whole life has never once looked back—he will surely become a vessel of great weight."
translations.idiomatic: Hao's mother often told those close to her, "This boy has never once looked back in his life—he will surely become someone of great consequence."

sentences.zh: 」及長，沉深有行檢，不妄通賓客。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was deep and steady and had conduct of restraint; he did not rashly receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was sober and principled and did not receive guests casually.

sentences.zh: 魏大統中，釋褐著作郎，遷太子洗馬、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Great Unity era of Wei he doffed his commoner's garb as Master of Writings, was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent and Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Wei's Datong era he entered office as Master of Writings, then was promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent and supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 周受禪，拜平東將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Zhou received the abdication, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Zhou took the throne he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 于時貴公子皆競習弓馬，被服多為軍容。

translations.literal: At that time noble sons all vied in practicing bow and horse; their dress was mostly in military style.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sons of the nobility all competed in horsemanship and archery, and dressed mostly in military fashion.

sentences.zh: 禮成雖善騎射，而從容儒服，不失素望。

translations.literal: Although Licheng excelled at riding and shooting, he wore scholar's robes with ease and did not lose his original reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Although Licheng was skilled at riding and archery, he still wore scholar's robes with ease and did not lose the reputation he had always enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，賜爵修陽縣侯，拜遷州刺史。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Yitong of the Third Rank, granted the title Marquis of Xiuyang county, and appointed Governor of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Yitong of the Third Rank, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuyang county, and appointed governor of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷有所徵發，禮成度以蠻夷不可擾，擾必為亂，上表固諫。

translations.literal: At that time the court had requisitions and levies; Licheng judged that the barbarians could not be disturbed—if disturbed they would surely rebel—and submitted a memorial firmly remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When the court issued requisitions, Licheng judged that the tribal peoples could not be disturbed without provoking rebellion and submitted a firm memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 周武帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 伐齊之役，從帝圍晉陽，禮成以兵擊南門，齊將席毗羅率精甲數千拒帝，禮成力戰，擊退之。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Qi he followed the Emperor in besieging Jinyang; Licheng led troops to attack the south gate. The Qi general Xi Piluo led several thousand elite armored troops to resist the Emperor; Licheng fought fiercely and beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Qi he followed the Emperor in the siege of Jinyang and led troops against the south gate. The Qi general Xi Piluo led several thousand elite armored troops to block the Emperor; Licheng fought hard and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 加開府，進封冠軍縣公，拜北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was given the privilege of an independent command, advanced to Duke of Guanjun county, and appointed Governor of North Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an independent command, promoted to Duke of Guanjun county, and appointed governor of North Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征為民部中大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and made Grand Master of the Ministry of the People.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to court as Grand Master of the Ministry of the People.

sentences.zh: 禮成妻竇氏早沒，知高祖有非常之表，遂聘高祖妹為繼室，情契甚歡。

translations.literal: Licheng's wife, the Lady Dou, had died early; knowing that Emperor Gaozu had an extraordinary bearing, he thereupon betrothed Gaozu's younger sister as his second wife; their affection and bond were very joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng's wife, of the Dou clan, had died early; recognizing that Yang Jian had the bearing of a man destined for greatness, he took Gaozu's younger sister as his second wife, and the two were deeply attached.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，進位上大將軍，遷司武上大夫，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Licheng was advanced to Supreme Grand General, transferred to Grand Master of the Ministry of War, and entrusted as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, Licheng was promoted to Supreme Grand General and Grand Master of the Ministry of War and entrusted as one of his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜陝州刺史，進封絳郡公，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Licheng was appointed Governor of Shanzhou, advanced to Duke of Jiang commandery, and given rewards generous and ample.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Licheng was appointed governor of Shanzhou, promoted to Duke of Jiang commandery, and showered with generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 尋征為左衛將軍，遷右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he was summoned as General of the Left Guards and transferred to Grand General of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as General of the Left Guards and promoted to Grand General of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出拜襄州總管，稱有惠政。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out and was appointed Governor-General of Xiangzhou; he was said to have had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was sent out as governor-general of Xiangzhou, where his rule was praised as benevolent.

sentences.zh: 後數載，複為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Several years later he again became Grand General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he again became Grand General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為寇患，緣邊要害，多委重臣，由是拜甯州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly made raids and calamity; the strategic points along the border were mostly entrusted to great ministers—therefore he was appointed Governor of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks raided repeatedly, and the key border posts were usually entrusted to senior ministers; for this reason he was appointed governor of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾征還京師，終於家。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled to the capital on account of illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was recalled to the capital because of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 其子世師，官至度支侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Shishi reached the office of Vice Minister of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi rose to the post of Vice Minister of the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: ○元孝矩弟褒

translations.literal: ○ Yuan Xiaoju; his younger brother Bao
translations.idiomatic: ● Yuan Xiaoju and his younger brother Bao

sentences.zh: 元孝矩，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiaoju was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiaoju came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖修義，父子均，並為魏尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiuyi and his father Zijun were both Vice Chancellors of the Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuyi and his father Zijun had both served as Vice Chancellors of the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 孝矩西魏時襲爵始平縣公，拜南豐州刺史。

translations.literal: In Western Wei Xiaoju inherited the title Duke of Shiping county and was appointed Governor of Nanfengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Western Wei, Xiaoju inherited the title Duke of Shiping county and was appointed governor of Nanfengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時見周太祖專政，將危元氏，孝矩每慨然有興複社稷之志，陰謂昆季曰：「昔漢氏有諸呂之變，硃虛、東牟，卒安劉氏。

translations.literal: At that time he saw the Zhou Founding Emperor monopolize government and endanger the Yuan clan; Xiaoju often sighed with resolve to restore the altars of state, and secretly told his brothers: "In the past the Han house had the trouble of the various Lüs; Zhu Xu and Dong Mou in the end settled the Liu clan."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Zhou Founding Emperor monopolize power and endanger the Yuan clan, Xiaoju often burned with the wish to restore the dynasty, and secretly told his brothers, "When the Han house faced the crisis of the Lü clan, Zhu Xu and Dong Mou in the end secured the Liu line."

sentences.zh: 今宇文之心，路人所見，顛而不扶，焉用宗子？

translations.literal: "Now Yuwen's heart is what every passerby sees; when the house is overturned and not propped up, of what use are imperial clansmen?"
translations.idiomatic: "Yuwen's intentions are plain to every passerby; when the house is falling and no one steadies it, what use are we imperial clansmen?"

sentences.zh: 盍將圖之？

translations.literal: "Why not plot against him?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why not act against him?"

sentences.zh: 」為兄則所遏，孝矩乃止。

translations.literal: He was stopped by his elder brother Ze, and Xiaoju desisted.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ze stopped him, and Xiaoju gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 其後周太祖為兄子晉公護娶孝矩妹為妻，情好甚密。

translations.literal: Later the Zhou Founding Emperor had his nephew the Duke of Jin, Yuwen Hu, marry Xiaoju's younger sister as his wife; their affection was very close.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Zhou Founding Emperor had his nephew Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin, marry Xiaoju's younger sister; the two became very close.

sentences.zh: 及閔帝受禪，護總百揆，孝矩之寵益隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min received the abdication, Hu held all government affairs, and Xiaoju's favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne, Hu held all government affairs, and Xiaoju's favor grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，坐徙蜀。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Xiaoju was implicated and exiled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was executed, Xiaoju was implicated and exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 數戰，征還京師，拜益州總管司馬，轉司憲大夫。

translations.literal: After several campaigns he was recalled to the capital, appointed Chief Administrator under the Governor-General of Yizhou, and transferred to Grand Master of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After several campaigns he was recalled to the capital, appointed chief administrator under the governor-general of Yizhou, and later transferred to Grand Master of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 高祖重其門地，娶其女為房陵王妃。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu valued his lineage and married his daughter to the Prince of Fangling as princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu valued his family standing and married his daughter to the Prince of Fangling.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，拜少塚宰，進位柱國，賜爵洵陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Xiaoju was appointed Junior Director of the Mausoleum, advanced to Pillar of State, and granted the title Duke of Xunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, Xiaoju was appointed Junior Director of the Mausoleum, promoted to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時房陵王鎮洛陽，及上受禪，立為皇太子，令孝矩代鎮。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Fangling garrisoned Luoyang; when the Emperor received the abdication and established him as Crown Prince, he ordered Xiaoju to replace him in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Fangling was posted to Luoyang; when Gaozu took the throne and made him crown prince, he had Xiaoju take his place as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 既而立其女為皇太子妃，親禮彌厚。

translations.literal: Then his daughter was established as Crown Princess, and intimate courtesy toward him grew all the thicker.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was then made crown princess, and the family's favor with the throne grew even deeper.

sentences.zh: 俄拜夀州總管，賜孝矩璽書曰：「揚、越氛昆，侵軼邊鄙，爭桑興役，不識大猷。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor-General of Shouzhou, and granted an imperial patent saying: "The vapors of Yang and Yue are chaotic; they invade and overrun the border marches, wrangling over mulberry fields and raising levies, ignorant of the great design."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Shouzhou, with an imperial patent reading, "Turmoil spreads through Yang and Yue; the borders are overrun, petty quarrels and levies abound, and the greater design is forgotten."

sentences.zh: 以公志存遠略，今故鎮邊服，懷柔以禮，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: "Because you, sir, keep far-reaching plans in mind, We now station you on the border to soothe them with courtesy—this matches Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: "Because you hold to a far-reaching vision, We now post you on the frontier to win them with courtesy and restraint—this is exactly what We intend."

sentences.zh: 」時陳將任蠻奴等屢寇江北，複以孝矩領行軍總管，屯兵于江上。

translations.literal: At that time the Chen generals Ren Mannu and others repeatedly raided north of the Yangtze; again Xiaoju was made campaigning commander-in-chief and stationed troops on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen generals such as Ren Mannu repeatedly raided north of the Yangtze, Xiaoju was again made campaigning commander-in-chief and stationed troops along the river.

sentences.zh: 後數載，自以年老，筋力漸衰，不堪軍旅，上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Several years later, considering himself old and his strength gradually declining, unable to bear military service, he submitted a memorial begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, finding himself old and his strength failing, unable to bear military duty, he memorialized asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 轉涇州刺史，高祖下書曰：「知執謙捴，請歸初服。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Jingzhou; Gaozu issued a document saying: "Knowing you hold humility and yield, you request return to your original garb."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Jingzhou; Gaozu wrote, "I know you hold to humility and ask to return to private life."

sentences.zh: 恭膺寶命，實賴元功，方欲委裘，寄以分陝，何容便請高蹈，獨為君子者乎！

translations.literal: "Reverently receiving the precious mandate, We truly rely on founding merit; We were about to lay aside the robe and entrust you with Fen and Shan—how can you at once request lofty withdrawal and alone become a gentleman of leisure!"
translations.idiomatic: "In taking up the throne I rely on men of founding merit; I was about to entrust you with the weight of the realm—how can you ask at once to withdraw and live only as a private gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 若以邊境務煩，即宜徙節涇郡，養德臥治也。

translations.literal: "If because border affairs are vexatious, then you should remove your command to Jing commandery and nurture virtue while governing from repose."
translations.idiomatic: "If the frontier duties are too burdensome, then move your command to Jing commandery and govern from repose while cultivating your strength."

sentences.zh: 」在州歲餘，卒官，年五十九。

translations.literal: After more than a year in office he died in post, at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jian (Simple).

sentences.zh: 子無竭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wujie had no heir.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wujie left no heir.

sentences.zh: 孝矩兄子文郁，見《誠節傳》。

translations.literal: Xiaoju's nephew's son Wenyu is treated in the "Biographies of Loyalty and Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoju's nephew's son Wenyu is treated in the Biographies of Loyalty and Integrity.

sentences.zh: 孝矩次弟雅，字孝方，有文武幹用。

translations.literal: Xiaoju's next younger brother Ya, courtesy name Xiaofang, had both literary and military ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoju's next younger brother Ya, whose courtesy name was Xiaofang, possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，曆左領左右將軍、集沁二州刺史，封順陽郡公。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he successively held the posts of General of the Left Guards, Governors of Ji and Qin, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign he served successively as General of the Left Guards and governor of Ji and Qin provinces, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 季弟褒，最知名。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Bao was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Bao was the most famous of the family.

sentences.zh: 褒字孝整，便弓馬，少有成人之量。

translations.literal: Bao, courtesy name Xiaozheng, was skilled at bow and horse and from youth had the measure of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, whose courtesy name was Xiaozheng, was skilled at horsemanship and archery and even as a boy showed the capacity of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 年十歲而孤，為諸兄所鞠養。

translations.literal: At ten years he was orphaned and was raised by his various elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at ten, he was raised by his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 性友悌，善事諸兄。

translations.literal: His nature was friendly and deferential, and he was good at serving his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He was affectionate and deferential by nature and devoted himself to his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 諸兄議欲別居，褒泣諫不得，家素富，多金寶，褒無所受，脫身而出，為州裡所稱。

translations.literal: His elder brothers discussed wishing to live separately; Bao wept and remonstrated but could not prevail. The family was from of old wealthy, with much gold and treasure; Bao accepted none of it, stripped himself and went out, and was praised by the district.
translations.idiomatic: When his brothers proposed dividing the household, Bao wept and pleaded in vain. The family was wealthy and held much gold and treasure, but Bao took none of it and left empty-handed—a conduct praised throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 及長，寬仁大度，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was generous and magnanimous and ranged through books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was generous and magnanimous and read widely in books and histories.

sentences.zh: 仕周，官至開府、北平縣公、趙州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Zhou and reached the offices of Independent Command, Duke of Beiping county, and Governor of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou he rose to an independent command, the title Duke of Beiping county, and the governorship of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉迥，以功超拜柱國，進封河間郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuchi Jiong; for merit he was leap-promoted to Pillar of State, advanced to Duke of Hejian commandery, with a fief of 2,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Jiong; for his merit he was promoted in one step to Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian commandery with a fief of 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，拜安州總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor-General of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang he was appointed governor-general of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徙原州總管。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Governor-General of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was transferred to governor-general of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 有商人為賊所劫，其人疑同宿者而執之，褒察其色冤而辭正，遂舍之。

translations.literal: A merchant was robbed by bandits; the man suspected a fellow lodger and seized him. Bao observed that his expression was aggrieved and his words upright, and thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant was robbed by bandits and seized a fellow lodger he suspected; Bao saw that the man's face showed distress and his words rang true, and released him.

sentences.zh: 商人詣闕訟褒受金縱賊，上遣使窮治之。

translations.literal: The merchant went to the court to sue, accusing Bao of taking gold to release the bandit; the Emperor sent an envoy to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant went to court accusing Bao of taking a bribe to release the thief; the Emperor sent an envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 使者簿責褒曰：「何故利金而舍盜也？

translations.literal: The envoy rebuked Bao on the register, saying: "Why profit from gold and release the thief?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy pressed him in the record, saying, "Why take gold and let the thief go?"

sentences.zh: 」褒便即引咎，初無異詞。

translations.literal: Bao immediately took the blame and from the start had no different words.
translations.idiomatic: Bao at once accepted the blame and offered no defense.

sentences.zh: 使者與褒俱詣京師，遂坐免官。

translations.literal: The envoy and Bao both went to the capital, and he was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy brought Bao to the capital, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 其盜尋發於他所，上謂褒曰：「公朝廷舊人，位望隆重，受金舍盜非善事，何至自誣也？

translations.literal: The thief was soon discovered in another place. The Emperor said to Bao: "You, sir, are an old man of the court, your position and renown weighty—taking gold and releasing the thief is no good affair; why go so far as to falsely accuse yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: The thief was soon caught elsewhere. The Emperor said to Bao, "You are a veteran of the court, a man of weight and standing—taking a bribe to free a thief would be a serious matter; why falsely accuse yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣受委一州，不能息盜賊，臣之罪一也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant received charge of one province and could not still the bandits—my first crime."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I was entrusted with a whole province and could not suppress banditry—that is my first offense."

sentences.zh: 州民為人所謗，不付法司，懸即放免，臣之罪二也。

translations.literal: "A man of the province was slandered by someone; I did not hand him to the law office but immediately released him—my second crime."
translations.idiomatic: "A subject of the province was slandered, and I did not send the case to the courts but released him at once—that is my second offense."

sentences.zh: 牽率愚誠，無顧形跡，不恃文書約束，至令為物所疑，臣之罪三也。

translations.literal: "Led by sincere foolishness, I disregarded appearances, did not rely on documentary constraints, and came to be suspected by others—my third crime."
translations.idiomatic: "Led by my own sincerity, I paid no heed to appearances or formal procedure, and so came under suspicion—that is my third offense."

sentences.zh: 臣有三罪，何所逃責？

translations.literal: "Your servant has three crimes—where can I escape blame?"
translations.idiomatic: "I have three offenses—how can I escape blame?"

sentences.zh: 臣又不言受賂，使者複將有所窮究，然則縲絏橫及良善，重臣之罪，是以自誣。

translations.literal: "Your servant also did not say I had taken a bribe; the envoy would further pursue the investigation, and then bonds would extend across good people—a heavy minister's crime—therefore I falsely accused myself."
translations.idiomatic: "If I denied taking a bribe, the envoy would press the inquiry further and innocent people would be dragged into bonds—that would be the greater fault of a senior minister, and so I accused myself."

sentences.zh: 」上歎異之，稱為長者。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in wonder and called him an elder worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marveled and called him a man of true stature.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以行軍總管屯兵備邊。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as campaigning commander-in-chief he stationed troops to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he served as campaigning commander-in-chief, stationing troops to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，複以行軍總管從漢王至柳城而還。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he again served as campaigning commander-in-chief, following the Prince of Han to Liucheng and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he again served as campaigning commander-in-chief, following the Prince of Han to Liucheng and back.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，嘉州夷、獠為寇，褒率步騎二萬擊平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou the Yi and Liao of Jiazhou made raids; Bao led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry and attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou reign the Yi and Liao of Jiazhou rebelled; Bao led twenty thousand foot and horse and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜齊州刺史，尋改為齊郡太守，吏民安之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Bao was appointed Governor of Qizhou, soon changed to Grand Administrator of Qi commandery; officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Bao was appointed governor of Qizhou, then grand administrator of Qi commandery, where officials and people lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 及興遼東之役，郡官督事者前後相屬，有西曹掾當行，詐疾，褒詰之，掾理屈，褒杖之，掾遂大言曰：「我將詣行在所，欲有所告。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign was launched, county officials overseeing tasks came one after another in succession. A West Bureau clerk who was due to go feigned illness; Bao interrogated him, the clerk was cornered in argument, and Bao caned him. The clerk then shouted loudly: "I am going to the mobile court and wish to make a report."
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign began, county officials overseeing the levy came in an unbroken stream. A clerk of the West Bureau who was due to depart feigned illness; Bao questioned him, the clerk was cornered, and Bao had him beaten. The clerk then shouted, "I am going to the imperial camp to lodge a complaint."

sentences.zh: 」褒大怒，因杖百餘，數日而死，坐是免官。

translations.literal: Bao was greatly angry and thereupon caned him more than a hundred times; he died several days later, and Bao was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Bao flew into a rage and had him beaten more than a hundred strokes; the clerk died several days later, and Bao was dismissed for it.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，時年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at home at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: ○郭榮

translations.literal: ○ Guo Rong
translations.idiomatic: ● Guo Rong

sentences.zh: 郭榮，字長榮，自雲太原人也。

translations.literal: Guo Rong, courtesy name Changrong, claimed origin in Taiyuan in Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Rong, whose courtesy name was Changrong, claimed descent from Taiyuan in Yun.

sentences.zh: 父徽，魏大統末為同州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Hui at the end of the Northern Wei's Great Unity era was Chief Administrator of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served at the end of the Northern Wei's Datong era as chief administrator of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時武元皇帝為刺史，由是與高祖有舊。

translations.literal: At that time the Martial Yuan Emperor was governor, and thereby had old ties with Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wu of Northern Wei was governor there, and through this the family formed old ties with Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 徽後官至洵州刺史、安城縣公。

translations.literal: Hui later reached the offices of Governor of Xunzhou and Duke of Ancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Hui later rose to governor of Xunzhou and Duke of Ancheng county.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，拜太僕卿，數年，卒官。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Grand Minister of Stud; several years later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Grand Minister of Stud; several years later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 榮容貌魁岸，外疏內密，與其交者多愛之。

translations.literal: Rong's appearance was lofty; outwardly open, inwardly close—those who associated with him mostly loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was imposing in appearance, open in manner but inwardly reserved; those who knew him tended to love him.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為親信。

translations.literal: The Zhou Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu took him as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu took him into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 護察榮謹厚，擢為中外府水曹參軍。

translations.literal: Hu observed that Rong was prudent and thick, and promoted him to adjutant in the Central-Outer Office's Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Hu saw that Rong was prudent and reliable and promoted him to adjutant in the Central-Outer Office's Water Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時齊寇屢侵，護令榮於汾州觀賊形勢。

translations.literal: At that time Qi raiders invaded repeatedly; Hu ordered Rong to observe the enemy's situation at Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi forces raided repeatedly, Hu sent Rong to Fenzhou to observe the enemy's movements.

sentences.zh: 時汾州與姚襄鎮相去懸遠，榮以為二城孤迥，勢不相救，請於州鎮之間更築一城，以相控攝，護從之。

translations.literal: At that time Fenzhou and Yaoxiang garrison were far apart in suspension; Rong judged the two cities isolated and distant, their forces unable to rescue each other, and requested building another city between prefecture and garrison to control and oversee each other; Hu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou and Yaoxiang garrison were far apart; Rong argued that the two posts were isolated and could not support each other, and proposed building a new city between them to link their defenses; Hu agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄而齊將段孝先攻陷姚襄、汾州二城，唯榮所立者獨能自守。

translations.literal: Shortly the Qi general Duan Xiaoxian attacked and took Yaoxiang and Fenzhou; only the city Rong had built could hold on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Qi general Duan Xiaoxian captured Yaoxiang and Fenzhou; only the city Rong had built held out.

sentences.zh: 護作浮橋，出兵渡河，與孝先戰。

translations.literal: Hu built a pontoon bridge, sent troops across the river, and fought Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Hu built a pontoon bridge, crossed the river with his army, and fought Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 孝先於上流縱大筏以擊浮橋，護令榮督便水者引取其筏。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian upstream released large rafts to strike the pontoon bridge; Hu ordered Rong to supervise skilled watermen to draw off and seize the rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian sent large rafts downstream to smash the pontoon bridge; Hu had Rong direct skilled watermen to seize the rafts.

sentences.zh: 以功授大都督。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 護又以稽胡數為寇亂，使榮綏集之。

translations.literal: Hu also because the Ji Hu repeatedly made raids and disorder, sent Rong to pacify and gather them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Ji Hu raided repeatedly, Hu also sent Rong to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 榮于上郡、延安築周昌、弘信、廣安、招遠、咸寧等五城，以遏其要路，稽胡由是不能為寇。

translations.literal: Rong at Shangjun and Yan'an built five cities—Zhouchang, Hongxin, Guang'an, Zhaoyuan, and Xianning—to block their key routes; thereby the Ji Hu could not make raids.
translations.idiomatic: Rong built five cities at Shangjun and Yan'an—Zhouchang, Hongxin, Guang'an, Zhaoyuan, and Xianning—to block their main routes, and the Ji Hu could no longer raid.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，拜宣納中士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally handled all affairs, Rong was appointed Xuanna Central Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal charge of government, Rong was appointed Xuanna Central Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後從帝平齊，以戰功，賜馬二十匹，綿絹六百段，封平陽縣男，遷司水大夫。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for war merit he was granted twenty horses and six hundred lengths of silk, enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang county, and transferred to Grand Master of the Water Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the Emperor in the pacification of Qi; for his military merit he received twenty horses and six hundred lengths of silk, was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang county, and promoted to Grand Master of the Water Ministry.

sentences.zh: 榮少與高祖親狎，情契極歡，嘗與高祖夜坐月下，因從容謂榮曰：「吾仰觀玄象，俯察人事，周曆已盡，我其代之。

translations.literal: Rong from youth was intimate with Gaozu, their bond of affection extreme in joy. Once he sat with Gaozu at night under the moon and at leisure said to Rong: "I look up and observe the dark signs, look down and examine human affairs—the Zhou mandate is ended; I shall replace it."
translations.idiomatic: Rong had been close to Yang Jian since youth, and their bond ran very deep. One night they sat together under the moon, and Yang Jian said frankly to him, "I read the heavens above and human affairs below—the Zhou mandate is spent, and I shall take its place."

sentences.zh: 」榮深自結納。

translations.literal: Rong deeply bound himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong pledged himself to him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，高祖總百揆，召榮，撫其背而笑曰：「吾言驗未？

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Gaozu held all government affairs, summoned Rong, patted his back and laughed, saying: "Were my words verified or not?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died and Yang Jian took control of government, he summoned Rong, clapped him on the back, and laughed, "Have my words come true?"

sentences.zh: 」即拜相府樂曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed adjutant in the Chancellor's Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed adjutant in the Chancellor's Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官複領蕃部大夫。

translations.literal: Shortly, retaining his original office, he also headed the Tribal Affairs Grand Master post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, while keeping his original post, he also took charge of tribal affairs as Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，引為內史舍人，以龍潛之舊，進爵蒲城郡公，加位上儀同。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was brought in as Inner Secretariat Attendant; for old ties from the dragon in hiding, he was advanced to Duke of Pucheng commandery and given the rank Supreme Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Inner Secretariat Attendant; for their bond from the years before he rose, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pucheng commandery and given the rank Supreme Yitong.

sentences.zh: 累遷通州刺史。

translations.literal: He was successively transferred to Governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，西南夷、獠多叛，詔榮領八州諸軍事行軍總管，率兵討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou the Yi and Liao of the southwest rebelled in great numbers; an edict ordered Rong to lead the military affairs of eight provinces as campaigning commander-in-chief and lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou reign many Yi and Liao of the southwest rebelled; Rong was ordered to serve as campaigning commander-in-chief over eight provinces and lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 歲餘悉平，賜奴婢三百餘口。

translations.literal: After more than a year all were pacified; he was granted more than three hundred servants.
translations.idiomatic: Within a little over a year all were pacified, and he was granted more than three hundred servants.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，入為武候驃騎將軍，以嚴正聞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Rong entered court as Flying Cavalry General of the Martial Guards and was known for stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Rong entered court as Flying Cavalry General of the Martial Guards and was known for his stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，黔安首領田羅駒阻清江作亂，夷陵諸郡，民夷多應者，詔榮擊平之。

translations.literal: Several years later the Qian'an chieftain Tian Luoju blocked the Qing River and made disorder; in the commanderies around Yiling, commoners and Yi mostly responded; an edict ordered Rong to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the Qian'an chieftain Tian Luoju blocked the Qing River in rebellion; in the commanderies around Yiling many commoners and tribal peoples joined him, and Rong was ordered to attack and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 遷左候衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 從帝西征吐谷渾，拜銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor on the western expedition against Tuyuhun and was appointed Silver-Green Grand Counselor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Emperor on the western expedition against Tuyuhun and was appointed Silver-Green Grand Counselor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以功進位左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, for merit he was advanced to Left Grand Counselor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Left Grand Counselor of the Palace for his merit.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝複事遼東，榮以為中國疲敝，萬乘不宜屢動，乃言於帝曰：「戎狄失禮，臣下之事。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor again undertook Liaodong; Rong judged that China was weary and exhausted, and the Son of Heaven should not move frequently, and spoke to the Emperor, saying: "When the barbarians lose ritual propriety, that is a matter for ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Emperor again launched a Liaodong campaign; Rong believed the empire was exhausted and the Son of Heaven should not march out repeatedly, and told the Emperor, "When barbarians break ritual propriety, that is work for his ministers."

sentences.zh: 臣聞千鈞之弩不為鼷鼠發機，豈有親辱大駕以臨小寇？

translations.literal: "Your servant has heard that a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its trigger for a mouse—how could there be personally dishonoring the great carriage to face small bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that a crossbow of a thousand jun is not drawn for a mouse—why should Your Majesty personally humble the imperial carriage to face a petty foe?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 複從軍攻遼東城，榮親蒙矢石，晝夜不釋甲胄百餘日。

translations.literal: Again he followed the army in attacking Liaodong city; Rong personally exposed himself to arrows and stones, day and night not removing armor for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the army in the attack on Liaodong city; Rong personally braved arrows and stones and did not remove his armor day or night for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 帝每令人窺諸將所為，知榮如是，帝大悅，每勞勉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor often sent men to spy on what the generals were doing; learning that Rong was like this, the Emperor was greatly pleased and always comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often had observers watch what his generals were doing; when he learned how Rong conducted himself, he was greatly pleased and repeatedly praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 九年，帝至東都，謂榮曰：「公年德漸高，不宜久涉行陣，當與公一郡，任所選也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor came to the Eastern Capital and said to Rong: "Your years and virtue are gradually high; you should not long involve yourself in marching columns. We shall give you one commandery—you may choose which."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Emperor came to the Eastern Capital and told Rong, "You are growing old and should not remain long in the field; I shall give you a commandery of your own choosing."

sentences.zh: 」榮不願違離，頓首陳讓，辭情哀苦，有感帝心，於是拜為右候衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Rong was unwilling to part; he prostrated himself and declined, his words grieving and bitter, moving the Emperor's heart; thereupon he was appointed Grand General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was unwilling to leave his side; he prostrated himself and pleaded to stay, his words so heartfelt that they moved the Emperor, who then appointed him Grand General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝謂百僚曰：「誠心純至如郭榮者，固無比矣。

translations.literal: Several days later the Emperor told the hundred officials: "One whose sincere heart is pure and utmost like Guo Rong's—in truth has no equal."
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the Emperor told the court, "For sincerity as pure and complete as Guo Rong's, there is truly no equal."

sentences.zh: 」其見信如此。

translations.literal: Such was the trust shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the trust the Emperor placed in him.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之亂，帝令馳守太原。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Yang Xuangan, the Emperor ordered him to ride swiftly to guard Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of Yang Xuangan, the Emperor ordered him to ride posthaste to defend Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，複從帝至柳城，遇疾，帝令存問動靜，中使相望。

translations.literal: The next year he again followed the Emperor to Liucheng, fell ill, and the Emperor ordered inquiries after his condition; palace envoys came one after another in sight of each other.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again followed the Emperor to Liucheng, fell ill, and the Emperor sent repeated inquiries; palace envoys came in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 卒于懷遠鎮，時年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at Huaiyuan garrison at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Huaiyuan garrison at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝為之廢朝，贈兵部尚書，諡曰恭，贈物千段。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspended court for him, posthumously appointed him Minister of War, gave the posthumous name Gong (Respectful), and granted a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspended court in mourning, posthumously appointed him Minister of War, gave him the posthumous name Gong (Respectful), and granted a thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 有子福善。

translations.literal: He had a son Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Fushan.

sentences.zh: ○龐晃

translations.literal: ○ Pang Huang
translations.idiomatic: ● Pang Huang

sentences.zh: 龐晃，字元顯，榆林人也。

translations.literal: Pang Huang, courtesy name Yuanxian, was a native of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Huang, whose courtesy name was Yuanxian, came from Yulin.

sentences.zh: 父虯，周驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qiu was General of Agile Cavalry of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu had been General of Agile Cavalry under the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 晃少以良家子，刺史杜達召補州都督。

translations.literal: Huang in youth, as a son of a good family, was summoned by Governor Du Da to fill the post of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, as the son of a respectable family, Huang was summoned by Governor Du Da to serve as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 周太祖既有關中，署晃大都督，領親信兵，常置左右。

translations.literal: After the Zhou Founding Emperor held Guanzhong, he appointed Huang Grand Commander, leading trusted troops, constantly placed at his side.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou Founding Emperor secured Guanzhong, he appointed Huang Grand Commander in charge of trusted troops and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 晃因徙居關中。

translations.literal: Huang thereupon moved his residence to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his household into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 後遷驃騎將軍，襲爵比陽侯。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry and inherited the title Marquis of Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and inherited the title Marquis of Biyang.

sentences.zh: 衛王直出鎮襄州，晃以本官從。

translations.literal: Prince Wei Zhi went out to garrison Xiangzhou; Huang followed in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Zhi was posted to garrison Xiangzhou, Huang accompanied him in his existing post.

sentences.zh: 尋與長湖西元定擊江南，孤軍深入，遂沒於陣。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Yuwen Ding of Changhu West in attacking the lands south of the Yangtze; the lone army advanced deep and was lost in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Yuwen Ding of Changhu West in an attack on the south; their isolated force pushed deep into enemy territory and was overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 數年，衛王直遣晃弟車騎將軍元俊齎絹八百匹贖焉，乃得歸朝。

translations.literal: Several years later Prince Wei Zhi sent Huang's younger brother, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yuwen Jun, bearing eight hundred lengths of silk to ransom him, and he was able to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Prince Wei Zhi sent Huang's younger brother Yuwen Jun, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with eight hundred lengths of silk to ransom him, and he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同，賜彩二百段，複事衛王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supreme Yitong, granted two hundred lengths of colored silk, and again served Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supreme Yitong, granted two hundred lengths of colored silk, and again served Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 時高祖出為隨州刺史，路經襄陽，衛王令晃詣高祖。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu went out as Governor of Suizhou; passing through Xiangyang, the prince ordered Huang to call on Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was sent out as governor of Suizhou and passed through Xiangyang, the prince had Huang call on him.

sentences.zh: 晃知高祖非常人，深自結納。

translations.literal: Huang knew Gaozu was no ordinary man and deeply bound himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang recognized that Yang Jian was no ordinary man and pledged himself to him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 及高祖去官歸京師，晃迎見高祖于襄邑。

translations.literal: When Gaozu left office and returned to the capital, Huang went to meet him at Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian left office and returned to the capital, Huang went to meet him at Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚歡，晃因白高祖曰：「公相貌非常，名在圖籙。

translations.literal: Gaozu was very pleased; Huang thereupon told Gaozu: "Your appearance is extraordinary; your name is in the charts and registers."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was delighted, and Huang told him frankly, "Your bearing is extraordinary, and your name is written in the charts of fate."

sentences.zh: 九五之日，幸願不忘。

translations.literal: "On the day of the Nine-Five, I hope you will not forget."
translations.idiomatic: "When you reach the throne, I hope you will not forget me."

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑曰：「何妄言也！

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "What wild talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian laughed and said, "What wild talk!"

sentences.zh: 」頃之，有一雄雉鳴于庭，高祖命晃射之，曰：「中則有賞。

translations.literal: Shortly a male pheasant cried in the courtyard; Gaozu ordered Huang to shoot it, saying: "If you hit it, there will be a reward."
translations.idiomatic: Before long a cock pheasant called in the courtyard; Yang Jian ordered Huang to shoot it, saying, "Hit it and you shall be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 然富貴之日，持以為驗。

translations.literal: "But on the day of wealth and honor, keep this as proof."
translations.idiomatic: "Keep this as proof for the day of your wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 」晃既射而中，高祖撫掌大笑曰：「此是天意，公能感之而中也。

translations.literal: Huang shot and hit it; Gaozu clapped his hands and laughed greatly, saying: "This is Heaven's intent—you were able to sense it and hit."
translations.idiomatic: Huang shot and hit it; Yang Jian clapped his hands and laughed, "This is Heaven's will—you sensed it and struck true."

sentences.zh: 」因以二婢賜之，情契甚密。

translations.literal: He thereupon gave him two maidservants; their bond of affection was very close.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Huang two maidservants, and their bond grew very close.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，晃為常山太守，高祖為定州總管，屢相往來。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu, Huang was Grand Administrator of Changshan and Gaozu was Governor-General of Dingzhou; they frequently visited each other.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu's reign Huang was grand administrator of Changshan while Yang Jian was governor-general of Dingzhou; the two visited each other often.

sentences.zh: 俄而高祖轉亳州總管，將行，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Shortly Gaozu was transferred to Governor-General of Bozhou; about to depart, he was very displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Jian was transferred to governor-general of Bozhou; as he prepared to leave, he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 晃因白高祖曰：「燕、代精兵之處，今若動眾，天下不足圖也。

translations.literal: Huang thereupon told Gaozu: "Yan and Dai are places of elite troops; if you now move the masses, the realm under Heaven is not enough to be plotted for."
translations.idiomatic: Huang told him frankly, "Yan and Dai are home to elite troops; if you raise an army now, the empire will be within your grasp."

sentences.zh: 」高祖握晃手曰：「時未可也。

translations.literal: Gaozu grasped Huang's hand and said: "The time is not yet possible."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian gripped his hand and said, "The time is not yet ripe."

sentences.zh: 」晃亦轉為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Huang was also transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was also promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為揚州總管，奏晃同行。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Governor-General of Yangzhou, he memorialized that Huang accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became governor-general of Yangzhou, he requested that Huang accompany him.

sentences.zh: 既而高祖為丞相，進晃位開府，命督左右，甚見親待。

translations.literal: Shortly Gaozu became Chancellor, advanced Huang to Independent Command, ordered him to supervise the left and right, and he was greatly favored and treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he promoted Huang to an independent command and put him in charge of his personal guard, treating him with exceptional intimacy.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，謂晃曰：「射雉之符，今日驗不？

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he said to Huang: "The sign of shooting the pheasant—is it verified today or not?"
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he said to Huang, "The omen of the pheasant—has it come true today?"

sentences.zh: 」晃再拜曰：「陛下應天順民，君臨宇內，猶憶曩時之言，不勝慶躍。

translations.literal: Huang bowed twice and said: "Your Majesty responds to Heaven and follows the people, ruling the realm within the four seas, yet still recalls words of old—I cannot bear the leap of celebration."
translations.idiomatic: Huang bowed twice and said, "Your Majesty has answered Heaven and won the people, ruling all within the seas, yet still remembers what was said in those days—I am overcome with joy."

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「公之此言，何得忘也！

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said: "How could We forget these words of yours!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and said, "How could I forget words like yours!"

sentences.zh: 」尋加上開府，拜右衛將軍，進爵為公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given Superior Independent Command, appointed General of the Right Guards, advanced in rank to Duke, with a fief of 1,500 households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given superior independent command, appointed General of the Right Guards, and promoted to duke with a fief of 1,500 households.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘之擊突厥也，晃以行軍總管從至馬邑。

translations.literal: When Prince Hejian Hong attacked the Turks, Huang as campaigning commander-in-chief followed to Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hejian of Hong attacked the Turks, Huang followed as campaigning commander-in-chief as far as Mayi.

sentences.zh: 別路出賀蘭山，擊賊破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: By a separate route he went out through Helan Mountain, struck the bandits and broke them, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By a separate route he marched through Helan Mountain, routed the enemy, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 晃性剛悍，時廣平王雄當途用事，勢傾朝廷，晃每陵侮之。

translations.literal: Huang's nature was fierce and overbearing; at that time Prince Guangping Xiong held power on the road of office and his influence tilted the court; Huang often insulted and humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was fierce and overbearing by nature; at that time Prince Guangping Xiong held power at court, and Huang often treated him with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 嘗於軍中臥，見雄不起，雄甚銜之。

translations.literal: Once he was lying in camp and, seeing Xiong, did not rise; Xiong deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once, lying in camp, he did not rise when he saw Xiong; Xiong deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 複與高熲有隙，二人屢譖晃。

translations.literal: He also had a rift with Gao Jiong; the two men repeatedly slandered Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a feud with Gao Jiong; the two repeatedly slandered him at court.

sentences.zh: 由是宿衛十餘年，官不得進。

translations.literal: Thereby for more than ten years in palace guard service his office could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he spent more than ten years in palace guard service without promotion.

sentences.zh: 出為懷州刺史，數歲，遷原州總管。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Huaizhou; several years later he was transferred to Governor-General of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Huaizhou; several years later he was transferred to governor-general of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中卒官，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he died in office at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office during the Renshou reign at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 高祖為之廢朝，贈物三百段，米三百石，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Gaozu suspended court for him, granted three hundred lengths of goods and three hundred shi of grain, and gave the posthumous name Jing (Respectful).
