translations.idiomatic: Gaozu suspended court in mourning, granted three hundred lengths of goods and three hundred shi of grain, and gave him the posthumous name Jing (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 子長壽，頗知名，官至驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His son Changshou was quite renowned and reached the office of General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changshou was well known and rose to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: ○李安

translations.literal: ○ Li An
translations.idiomatic: ● Li An

sentences.zh: 李安，字玄德，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Li An, courtesy name Xuande, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li An, whose courtesy name was Xuande, came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父蔚，仕周為朔燕恆三州刺史、襄武縣公。

translations.literal: His father Wei served Zhou as Governor of the three provinces Shuo, Yan, and Heng, and as Duke of Xiangwu county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei had served the Northern Zhou as governor of Shuo, Yan, and Heng provinces and as Duke of Xiangwu county.

sentences.zh: 安美姿儀，善騎射。

translations.literal: An had handsome bearing and was skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: An was handsome in bearing and skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 周天和中，釋褐右侍上士，襲爵襄武公。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era of Zhou he doffed commoner's garb as Right Attendant Senior Gentleman and inherited the title Duke of Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Zhou's Tianhe era he entered office as Right Attendant Senior Gentleman and inherited the title Duke of Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 俄授儀同、少師右上士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given Yitong rank and Junior Mentor Right Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given Yitong rank and appointed Junior Mentor Right Senior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，引之左右，遷職方中大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he brought An into his personal retinue and transferred him to Grand Master of the Ministry of Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, he brought An into his inner circle and promoted him to Grand Master of the Ministry of Offices.

sentences.zh: 複拜安弟悊為儀同。

translations.literal: An's younger brother Ti was also appointed Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: An's younger brother Ti was also appointed Yitong.

sentences.zh: 安叔父梁州刺史璋，時在京師，與周趙王謀害高祖，誘悊為內應。

translations.literal: An's uncle Zhang, Governor of Liangzhou, was then in the capital; with the Zhou Prince of Zhao he plotted to harm Gaozu and enticed Ti as an inside responder.
translations.idiomatic: An's uncle Zhang, governor of Liangzhou, was then in the capital; with the Zhou Prince of Zhao he plotted against Yang Jian and tried to win Ti as an inside accomplice.

sentences.zh: 悊謂安曰：「寢之則不忠，言之則不義，失忠與義，何以立身？

translations.literal: Ti said to An: "To conceal it is disloyalty; to speak of it is unrighteous—losing loyalty and righteousness, how can one stand in the world?"
translations.idiomatic: Ti said to An, "To conceal this is disloyalty; to report it seems unrighteous—without loyalty and righteousness, how can one stand in the world?"

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「丞相父也，其可背乎？

translations.literal: An said: "The Chancellor is as a father—how could one betray him?"
translations.idiomatic: An said, "The Chancellor is like a father to us—how could we betray him?"

sentences.zh: 」遂陰白之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: They then reported the plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 及趙王等伏誅，將加官賞，安頓首而言曰：「兄弟無汗馬之勞，過蒙獎擢，合門竭節，無以酬謝。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao and others were executed, as rewards and offices were about to be added, An prostrated himself and said: "We brothers have no labor of horses sweating; we have excessively received promotion and selection—the whole house exhausts its loyalty and has no means to repay thanks."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao and the others were executed and rewards were to be given, An prostrated himself and said, "We brothers have done no military service, yet we have been favored beyond measure; our whole house would give its utmost loyalty and still cannot repay such grace."

sentences.zh: 不意叔父無狀，為凶黨之所蠱惑，覆宗絕嗣，其甘若薺。

translations.literal: "We did not expect our uncle's misconduct, bewitched by the vicious faction, overthrowing the clan and cutting off heirs—as bitter as shepherd's purse."
translations.idiomatic: "We never expected our uncle's misconduct, led astray by villains to destroy the clan and cut off its line—a bitterness like shepherd's purse."

sentences.zh: 蒙全首領，為幸實多，豈可將叔父之命以求官賞？

translations.literal: "To be spared with our heads intact is already great fortune—how could we use our uncle's life to seek offices and rewards?"
translations.idiomatic: "To be spared with our lives is already great fortune—how could we trade on our uncle's fate for offices and rewards?"

sentences.zh: 」於是俯伏流涕，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he prostrated himself, weeping, grief beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: He then prostrated himself in tears, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 高祖為之改容曰：「我為汝特存璋子。

translations.literal: Gaozu changed expression for him and said: "For your sake I specially preserved Zhang's sons."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's expression changed as he said, "For your sake I have spared Zhang's sons."

sentences.zh: 」乃命有司罪止璋身，高祖亦為安隱其事而不言。

translations.literal: He then ordered the authorities that guilt stop at Zhang's person; Gaozu also concealed the affair for An and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that punishment fall on Zhang alone, and for An's sake he kept the matter quiet.

sentences.zh: 尋授安開府，進封趙郡公，悊上儀同、黃台縣男。

translations.literal: Shortly An was given Independent Command and advanced to Duke of Zhao commandery; Ti was given Supreme Yitong and made Baron of Huangtai county.
translations.idiomatic: Before long An was granted an independent command and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao commandery; Ti was made Supreme Yitong and Baron of Huangtai county.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，授安內史侍郎，轉尚書左丞、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, An was appointed Vice Minister of the Inner Secretariat, transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, An was appointed Vice Minister of the Inner Secretariat, then Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以為楊素司馬，仍領行軍總管，率蜀兵順流東下。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen he was made Chief Administrator under Yang Su, still heading as campaigning commander-in-chief, leading Shu troops downstream eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he served as chief administrator under Yang Su while also commanding as campaigning commander-in-chief, leading Shu troops downstream.

sentences.zh: 時陳人屯白沙，安謂諸將曰：「水戰非北人所長。

translations.literal: At that time the Chen forces were encamped at Baisha; An told the generals: "Water combat is not what northerners excel at."
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen forces were encamped at Baisha, An told the generals, "Water combat is not what northerners do best."

sentences.zh: 今陳人依險泊船，必輕我而無備。

translations.literal: "Now the Chen men moor their boats relying on perilous ground; they will surely underestimate us and be without preparation."
translations.idiomatic: "The Chen have anchored in a defensible spot and will surely underestimate us and leave themselves unguarded."

sentences.zh: 以夜襲之，賊可破也。

translations.literal: "Strike them by night and the bandits can be broken."
translations.idiomatic: "Attack them by night and they can be broken."

sentences.zh: 」諸將以為然。

translations.literal: The generals considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 安率眾先鋒，大破陳師。

translations.literal: An led the masses as vanguard and greatly defeated the Chen army.
translations.idiomatic: An led the vanguard and routed the Chen army.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，詔書勞曰：「陳賊之意，自言水戰為長，險隘之間，彌謂官軍所憚。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised him; an edict of commendation said: "The Chen bandits' intent—they themselves say water combat is their strength; in narrow and perilous places they all the more consider the government army to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him with an edict of commendation: "The Chen thought themselves masters of water combat and believed our army feared narrow waters."

sentences.zh: 開府親將所部，夜動舟師，摧破賊徒，生擒虜眾，益官軍之氣，破賊人之膽，副朕所委，聞以欣然。

translations.literal: "The Independent Commander personally led his command, moved the river forces by night, crushed and broke the bandit host, captured the enemy alive in numbers, increased the government army's spirit, broke the bandits' courage—fulfilling what We entrusted; on hearing it We are pleased."
translations.idiomatic: "You personally led your command, moved the fleet by night, crushed the enemy, took many prisoners, raised our army's spirit and broke the enemy's nerve—you have fulfilled what I entrusted to you, and I am delighted to hear it."

sentences.zh: 」進位上大將軍，除郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Supreme Grand General and appointed Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supreme Grand General and appointed governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 數日，轉鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: Several days later he was transferred to Governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was transferred to governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 安請為內職，高祖重違其意，除左領左右將軍。

translations.literal: An requested an inner-court post; Gaozu heavily went against his wish and appointed him General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: An asked for a post at court; Gaozu, reluctant to refuse him outright, appointed him General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右領軍大將軍，複拜悊開府儀同三司、備身將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Guards; Ti was again appointed Independent Command Yitong of the Third Rank and Personal Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Grand General of the Right Guards; Ti was again made Independent Command Yitong of the Third Rank and Personal Guard General.

sentences.zh: 兄弟俱典禁衛，恩信甚重。

translations.literal: The brothers together held charge of the forbidden guard; favor and trust were very weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers together commanded the palace guard and enjoyed exceptional favor and trust.

sentences.zh: 八年，突厥犯塞，以安為行軍總管，從楊素擊之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Turks violated the frontier; An was made campaigning commander-in-chief and followed Yang Su in striking them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Turks raided the frontier, An served as campaigning commander-in-chief under Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 安別出長川，會虜渡河，與戰破之。

translations.literal: An by a separate route went out through Changchuan, met the barbarians crossing the river, fought and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: An marched by a separate route through Changchuan, met the enemy as they crossed the river, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，出安為甯州刺史，悊為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, An went out as Governor of Ningzhou and Ti as Governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, An was sent out as governor of Ningzhou and Ti as governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 安子瓊，悊子瑋，始自繈褓，乳養宮中，至是年八九歲，始命歸家。

translations.literal: An's son Qiong and Ti's son Wei, from swaddling clothes, were nursed and reared in the palace; by now they were eight or nine years old, and only then were they ordered to return home.
translations.idiomatic: An's son Qiong and Ti's son Wei had been raised in the palace from infancy; only now, at eight or nine years of age, were they sent home.

sentences.zh: 其見親顧如是。

translations.literal: Such was the intimate regard shown them.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the intimacy and favor they enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗言及作相時事，因湣安兄弟滅親奉國，乃下詔曰：「先王立教，以義斷恩，割親愛之情，盡事君之道，用能弘獎大節，體此至公。

translations.literal: Gaozu once spoke of affairs when he was Chancellor; commiserating with An and his brother for destroying kin to serve the state, he issued an edict saying: "The former kings established teaching—by righteousness cutting off favor, severing feelings of kin love, exhausting the way of serving the ruler—thereby able to magnify and reward great principle, embodying this utmost public-mindedness."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once spoke of his time as Chancellor; moved by how An and his brother had sacrificed family ties to serve the state, he issued an edict: "The ancient kings taught that righteousness must cut through private affection, that one must set aside love of kin to fulfill loyalty to one's lord—only thus can great integrity be honored and true impartiality embodied."

sentences.zh: 往者周曆既窮，天命將及，朕登庸惟始，王業初基，承此澆季，實繁奸宄。

translations.literal: "In the past the Zhou mandate was already exhausted and the Heavenly mandate was about to arrive; We ascended employment at the very beginning, the royal enterprise just founded, inheriting this diluted season—in truth rife with traitors and villains."
translations.idiomatic: "When the Zhou mandate was spent and Heaven's mandate was passing to Us, We had only just begun to rise, the royal enterprise barely founded, in an age already rife with treachery."

sentences.zh: 上大將軍、甯州刺史、趙郡公李安，其叔璋潛結籓枝，扇惑猶子，包藏不逞，禍機將發。

translations.literal: "Supreme Grand General, Governor of Ningzhou, Duke of Zhao commandery Li An—his uncle Zhang secretly joined with feudal branches, fanned and deluded younger nephews, harbored unruly intent, and the omen of calamity was about to break forth."
translations.idiomatic: "Supreme Grand General, governor of Ningzhou, Duke of Zhao commandery Li An—his uncle Zhang secretly conspired with other princes, incited younger kinsmen, harbored rebellious intent, and disaster was about to break out."

sentences.zh: 安與弟開府儀同三司、衛州刺史、黃台縣男悊，深知逆順，披露丹心，凶謀既彰，罪人斯得。

translations.literal: "An and his younger brother Independent Command Yitong of the Third Rank, Governor of Weizhou, Baron of Huangtai county Ti deeply knew rebellion and obedience, disclosed their crimson hearts; once the vicious plot was manifest, the guilty were obtained."
translations.idiomatic: "An and his brother Ti, Independent Command Yitong of the Third Rank, governor of Weizhou, Baron of Huangtai county, knew right from wrong and laid bare their loyal hearts; once the plot was exposed, the guilty were seized."

sentences.zh: 朕每念誠節，嘉之無已，懋庸冊賞，宜不逾時。

translations.literal: "We each time recall their sincere principle and praise them without end; rewarding merit and registering rewards should not exceed the season."
translations.idiomatic: "We have long cherished their loyal devotion and wished to reward them without delay."

sentences.zh: 但以事涉其親，猶有疑惑，欲使安等名教之方，自處有地，朕常為思審，遂致淹年。

translations.literal: "But because the affair involved their kin, there was still doubt; wishing to let An and others in the sphere of name and teaching have ground to place themselves, We often reflected and examined, and thus it extended over years."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet because the affair involved their own kin, We hesitated, wishing to give An and his brother a proper place within the norms of morality; We reflected on this at length, and years passed."

sentences.zh: 今更詳按聖典，求諸往事，父子天性，誠孝猶不並立，況複叔侄恩輕，情禮本有差降，忘私奉國，深得正理，宜錄舊勳，重弘賞命。

translations.literal: "Now further examining in detail the sage classics and seeking in past affairs—father and son by Heaven's nature, sincere filial piety still cannot stand together; how much more uncle and nephew, where favor is light and feeling and ritual from the root have differences and descent—forgetting the private to serve the state deeply obtains the correct principle; it is fitting to record old merit and again extend reward and mandate."
translations.idiomatic: "Now, reviewing the sage classics and past precedents, We see that even between father and son true loyalty and filial piety cannot always coexist; how much less between uncle and nephew, where the bond is lighter. To forget private ties and serve the state is the right course; their old merit should be honored and rewards renewed."

sentences.zh: 」於是拜安、悊俱為柱國，賜縑各五千匹，馬百匹，羊千口。

translations.literal: Thereupon An and Ti were both appointed Pillars of State, granted five thousand lengths of silk each, a hundred horses, and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: An and Ti were both made Pillars of State, each granted five thousand lengths of silk, a hundred horses, and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 複以悊為備身將軍，進封順陽郡公。

translations.literal: Ti was again made Personal Guard General and advanced to Duke of Shunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was again made Personal Guard General and promoted to Duke of Shunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 安謂親族曰：「雖家門獲全，而叔父遭禍，今奉此詔，悲愧交懷。

translations.literal: An told his kin: "Although the household gate was preserved whole, our uncle suffered calamity; now receiving this edict, grief and shame fill the breast together."
translations.idiomatic: An told his kin, "Though our house was spared, our uncle met disaster; to receive this edict now fills me with grief and shame together."

sentences.zh: 」因歔欷悲感，不能自勝。

translations.literal: He thereupon sighed and wept in grief, unable to master himself.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and wept, overcome with emotion.

sentences.zh: 先患水病，於是疾甚而卒，時年五十三。

translations.literal: He had earlier suffered from water illness; now the illness grew severe and he died, at the age of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from edema; the illness now grew severe and he died, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 諡曰懷。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Huai (Cherishing).
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Huai (Cherishing).

sentences.zh: 子瓊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qiong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少子孝恭，最有名。

translations.literal: His youngest son Xiaogong was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Xiaogong was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 悊後坐事除名，配防嶺南，道病卒。

translations.literal: Later Ti was dismissed from the register on account of an affair, assigned to garrison defense in Lingnan, and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ti was stripped of rank for an offense, exiled to garrison duty in Lingnan, and died of illness on the way.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：宇文慶等，龍潛惟舊，疇昔親姻，或素盡平生之言，或早有腹心之托。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yu Wen Qing and the others were old companions from the dragon in hiding, kin by marriage in days past—some had long spoken their life's words, some had early received trust from the inner heart.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Yu Wen Qing and the others were old companions from before Yang Jian rose to power, linked by marriage in earlier days—some had long shared their deepest thoughts with him, some had early won his innermost trust.

sentences.zh: 沾雲雨之餘潤，照日月之末光，騁步天衢，與時升降。

translations.literal: They touched the remaining moisture of cloud and rain, were illumined by the last rays of sun and moon, galloped along the heavenly highway, rising and falling with the times.
translations.idiomatic: They shared in the bounty of his favor, caught the last gleam of his glory, and advanced along the imperial path, rising and falling with the fortunes of the age.

sentences.zh: 高位厚秩，貽厥後昆，優矣！

translations.literal: High positions and thick ranks—they bequeathed these to their later descendants. Excellent indeed!
translations.idiomatic: High office and rich rewards—they passed these on to their descendants. How fortunate!

sentences.zh: 皛幼養宮中，未聞教義，煬帝愛之不以禮，其能不及於此乎？

translations.literal: Xiao was reared in the palace from youth and never heard of teaching and righteousness; Emperor Yang loved him without observing ritual propriety—could his ability fail to reach only this?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was raised in the palace from boyhood without proper instruction; Emperor Yang favored him without restraint—was it any wonder his conduct fell no lower than it did?

sentences.zh: 安、悊之于高祖，未有君臣之分，陷其骨肉，使就誅夷，大義滅親，所聞異於此矣。

translations.literal: As for An and Ti toward Gaozu, there was not yet the distinction of ruler and minister; they brought their flesh-and-blood kin to ruin and made them go to execution and extinction. "Destroying kin for great righteousness"—what is heard differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: An and Ti toward Gaozu had not yet taken on the full form of ruler and subject; they destroyed their own flesh and blood and sent them to execution. The classic phrase "destroying kin for righteousness" means something quite different from this.

sentences.zh: 雖有悲悼，何損於侃。

translations.literal: Although there was grief and mourning, what does that detract from Kan?
translations.idiomatic: Their grief and mourning notwithstanding, how could this be spoken of in the same breath as Jia Kan?
